ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: According to the process shown in the diagram in which a certain estuary area changes from A to B, what kind of change might have occurred in sea level? <image1>
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the left side is A, and the right side is B. In diagram A, the river branches on the land, and the diagonally shaded water area in the lower right near the estuary is relatively small in scope, mainly limited to the outside of the coast. In diagram B, the diagonally shaded water area near the estuary has obviously expanded, and extends inland along the river-valley-like zone; part of the land area that was originally close to the estuary appears to be submerged by water. Then reason: from A to B, the estuary water area expands and seawater invades the land, which belongs to the manifestation of transgression or a river valley being submerged. This kind of sea-land change appearing in the estuary area indicates that the relative sea level has risen; as far as sea-level change is concerned, it may be sea-level rise.
